key_insight: This paper shows that LLMs trained with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards can still be surprisingly sensitive to prompt wording that should not change the answer. By identifying and suppressing high-drift token choices during decoding, the method improves reasoning accuracy.
problem_solved: It addresses the instability of RLVR-trained language models when task-irrelevant prompt features change, even though the underlying problem and correct answer stay the same.
method: Create semifactual prompt interventions that preserve the task and answer while changing surface wording.
Measure token-level sensitivity to identify which prompt tokens cause the largest prediction drift.
Suppress high-drift token candidates during decoding to reduce sensitivity and improve reasoning accuracy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical way to make reasoning models more robust to harmless prompt variations. It can improve reliability in evaluation and deployment settings where prompts are not perfectly standardized.
